A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPON. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, throughput, representation-analysis, injection-location, and quantization results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds calibration-transfer, baseline-comparison, scale-up, continual-pretraining, MoE, and pruning experiments.

M1.justification: The original SPON transformation, KL calibration, and inference-time bias folding remain. V2 substantially extends the procedure with continual pretraining that optimizes only SPON using next-token cross-entropy without activation sparsity during training, followed by sparse evaluation. It also implements SPON in expert down-projections for reduced-expert MoE inference (Section 4.1 and Appendices H/K).

E1.justification: V2 retains WikiText and the original six QA tasks, adds C4 calibration, and evaluates ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, BoolQ, PIQA, and Winogrande. These additions broaden the actual training-data and task coverage, independently of the larger model configurations.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with LaRoSA, WINA, R-Sparse, and WAS in Table 2; SparseGPT, RIA, Pruner-Zero, MaskLLM, and ARMOR in Figure 3; and LoRA and bias-only/BitFit alternatives. Fixed neuron pruning disappears. Wanda remains in the Llama3-8B comparison, but its other original backbone results are removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include 0–60% sparsity sweeps after continual pretraining, 32B/70B model evaluations, expert-budget sweeps, LoRA-rank sweeps, and layerwise CKA measurement. The quantization experiment is now described at 60% sparsity instead of 50% (v1 Section 3.7; v2 Section 5.5), although the curves appear retained; this establishes a reported-setting revision, not a rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds shared-neuron activity versus sequence length, C4-to-WikiText calibration transfer, CKA representation analysis, activation-versus-bias controls, LoRA-rank sensitivity, and robustness studies involving pretraining, reduced expert budgets, and weight pruning. The original injection-location analysis remains, while the t-SNE analysis is revised.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix G newly specifies minibatch CKA estimation using an unbiased HSIC estimator. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests; the addition does not establish increased experimental replication.

E6.justification: Shared original perplexity and six-task accuracy entries remain unchanged, and throughput differences are equivalent rounding. V2 adds extensive comparison, scale-up, pretraining, MoE, and pruning results, including C4-calibrated perplexities of 7.95 and 5.94. Reported Llama3-8B t-SNE shifts change from 8.48/8.12 for TEAL/SPON in v1 Figure 3 to 8.69/8.21 in v2 Figure 13. Some original pruning results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the constant-bias MSE argument with a softmax-KL Hessian/Fisher derivation using a local second-order Taylor approximation (Section 2.4 and Appendix B). It removes v1 Appendix A's structured-versus-unstructured expressivity proof, revises the generalization argument, and corrects the sparsification formula to threshold absolute activation magnitudes.

C1.justification: V2 elevates representational instability from a suggested explanation to an asserted cause of sparse-model degradation and concludes that spontaneity is essential for robust sparse computation. Its contributions now foreground a Fisher-weighted mechanism and representational alignment. The central performance-recovery and negligible-overhead claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations based on Fisher-sensitive directions and pretrained feature-subspace alignment, using them to distinguish SPON from direct bias learning and LoRA. It interprets MoE and pruning benefits as compensation for lost representational capacity. Appendix H explicitly limits pretraining evidence to continual-training simulations because of compute/data constraints, and Appendix K leaves integration with pretraining-time routing unresolved.

D1.justification: The original calibration learning rate, epochs, batch size, chunk length, hardware, and training times remain unchanged in Appendix C. V2 adds full-token sparsification disclosure, bias initialization and ensemble constraints, and MoE training details of one epoch at learning rate 1e-6. V1's explicit bitsandbytes quantization implementation detail is removed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against newer activation-sparsity methods, network pruners, and parameter-efficient adaptation approaches, adding relevant WINA, WAS, ARMOR, LoRA, BitFit, and SCAP citations. CKA and MoE literature also enters. Much of v1's neuroscience/LLM-parallel survey and its associated citations disappears, while the basic biological motivation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological exposition, experimental narrative, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 introduces separate discussion and ablation sections, relocates the injection and quantization studies, and reorganizes the appendices. The title, author list, terminology, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, redraws the method overview and radar charts, combines new CKA displays with t-SNE in Figure 5, and relocates the full revised t-SNE display to Figure 13. Numerous comparison, pretraining, MoE, and pruning plots and tables are added; retained tables and injection-location plots are reformatted.

improvement.justification: C4 calibration transfer, direct bias/LoRA controls, CKA, and larger-model/MoE evaluations strengthen v1's mainly TEAL-based validation. However, stronger interpretations limit the gain: Figure 8 reports only 70.13% versus 70.07% for SPON and rank-1 LoRA without run uncertainty, and Tables 7–9 contain regressions despite all-sparsity improvement claims. The local Fisher approximation and informal complexity discussion also do not establish the new necessity and no-overfitting assertions. The added controls provide a limited net improvement.
